Chapter 6: Sticking to the Knitting—The Value of Focus and Core Competence
When organizations start to grow and taste success, it’s pretty tempting to branch out into new, unfamiliar territory, isn’t it?
But here’s something you’ll notice about companies that really stand the test of time—they’ve got this unwavering discipline in what we call “sticking to the knitting.”
In simple terms, it means focusing on what they do best, and resisting the urge to chase every shiny opportunity that comes along.
Imagine a master craftsman—someone who’s spent years honing one particular skill until it’s second nature.
Instead of getting distracted by every new trend, that craftsman keeps refining and deepening their expertise. And because of that, they build a reputation for quality and reliability.
Well, organizations work the same way. The ones that excel keep their resources, talent, and attention locked in on the areas where they already have a proven track record and unique capabilities.
So, how does this focus actually show up in day-to-day business?
First, let’s talk about clear boundaries. The most successful companies have a sharp sense of what’s truly central to their mission—and they steer clear of distractions that could water down their efforts.
Next, there’s continuous improvement. These organizations don’t just rest on their laurels. They’re always looking for ways to get even better at what they do, investing in innovation and efficiency to strengthen their core business.
And then, you have selective expansion. When a growth opportunity pops up, the best companies always ask: “Does this play to our strengths?” If it does, they’ll go for it—but only if it complements what they already do well, instead of stretching them too thin.
Let’s put this into perspective with a couple of real-world examples. Think about a company that’s famous for its customer service. Instead of jumping into a totally unrelated industry, they expand only into markets where their legendary service gives them a real edge.
Or, picture a manufacturer who invests in cutting-edge technology to improve their flagship product line, rather than spreading themselves across unfamiliar products just for the sake of variety.
Now, don’t get me wrong—sticking to the knitting doesn’t mean avoiding all change or shying away from innovation. It’s really about being intentional. Making sure that any new initiative builds on what you’re already great at, and strengthens your organization’s identity.
When companies stay focused like this, they sidestep the dangers of overextending themselves. They keep their clarity, their momentum, and—most importantly—their edge in the market.
So, here’s the key takeaway: By sticking to the knitting, you’re not just playing it safe. You’re setting your organization up for long-term excellence and building a foundation that’s tough to beat.
